quotes.t: I was unsatisfied by the arguments put forward by many men to explain the excellence of human nature
and only slightly inferior, as David affirms, to the angels
ab angelis, teste Davide, paulo deminutum
These reasons are indeed great, but they are nonetheless not the principal ones
why then would we not find the angels themselves and the blessed choirs of heaven even more admirable
Cur enim non ipsos angelos et beatissimos caeli choros magis admiremur
He had already adorned the supercelestial region with intelligences, enlivened the heavenly globes with eternal souls
Supercelestem regionem mentibus decorarat; ethereos globos aeternis animis vegetarat
nor was there among the seats of the world any place for this contemplator of the universe
Every place was by then filled; all things had already been assigned to the highest, the middle, and the lowest orders
Iam plena omnia; omnia summis, mediis infimisque ordinibus fuerant distributa
If he cultivates his rational seeds, he will become a heavenly being. If he cultivates his intellectual seeds, he will be an angel and a son of God
si rationalia, caeleste evadet animal; si intellectualia, angelus erit et Dei filius

judged.justification: The angelic state is the top of a scale of what man may cultivate in himself, not a separate order he can only envy.
Makes the angel a stage on the way, not the goal: the final term is union with God in darkness.

quotes.t: even the most secret Hebrew theology at one time transforms holy Enoch into an angel of divinity
whom they call [ מטטרון ] Metatron
and at other times it reshapes other men into other spirits

judged.justification: Fixes the Kabbalistic Enoch-Metatron transformation as the model of human-to-angelic change in the Oration.

quotes.t: not the circular body that makes the heavens, but straightforward reason; not the separation from the body that makes an angel, but its spiritual intelligence
nec caelum orbiculatum corpus, sed recta ratio; nec sequestratio corporis, sed spiritalis intelligentia angelum facit

judged.justification: Defines the angelic by a mode of knowing, so that an embodied philosopher can qualify.
A rank above the heavenly creature of section 29, clothed in flesh.

quotes.t: let us fly off to the otherworldly court that is near to the most eminent Divinity

There, according to the sacred mysteries, seraphim, cherubim, and thrones occupy the first places; let us emulate their dignity and glory, unwilling as we are to yield to them and unable to endure second place
Ibi, ut sacra tradunt mysteria, Seraphin, Cherubin et Throni primas possident

judged.justification: Sets the emulation of the highest angels as the programme of the whole Oration.

quotes.t: If so we wish, we will not be inferior to them at all
Let us consider what they do, what life they lead
If we too live that life (and indeed we can), we will be equal to their lot
The seraph burns with the fire of love; the cherub shines with the splendour of intelligence; the throne stands in the steadfastness of judgment
Ardet Saraph charitatis igne; fulget Cherub intelligentiae splendore; stat Thronus iudicii firmitate

judged.justification: Assigns each of the three ranks one operation, love, intelligence, judgment, on which the rest of the passage builds.

quotes.t: if we, being dedicated to an active life, undertake the care of inferior things with proper consideration of their worth, we will be strengthened by the steadfast solidity of the thrones
Igitur si actuosae addicti vitae inferiorum curam recto examine susceperimus, Thronorum stata soliditate firmabimur
If we burn for the Creator alone, with charity, with its all-consuming fire, we shall burst into flame in the likeness of the seraphim
in Saraphicam effigiem repente flammabimur
Over the cherub, that is, over the contemplator, He flies and, as if brooding over him, imbues him with warmth
Super Cherub, idest contemplatore, volat atque eum quasi incubando fovet
He who is a seraph, that is, a lover, is in God and God is in him; indeed, he and God are one
Qui Saraph, idest amator est, in Deo est, et Deus in eo, immo et Deus et ipse unum sunt
Great is the power of the thrones that we may reach by judging; supreme is the height of the seraphim that we may reach by loving
And yet in what manner can anyone either judge or love things unknown?
Moses loved the Lord Whom he saw. As a judge, Moses administered to the people the things that he earlier saw on the mountain as a contemplator

judged.justification: Argues that knowing must precede both loving and judging, which is what puts the cherub in the middle.

quotes.t: the cherub, located in the middle position, uses his light both to prepare us for the seraphic fire and likewise to illuminate for us the judgment of the thrones
Ergo medius Cherub sua luce et Saraphico igni nos praeparat, et ad Thronorum iudicium pariter illuminat

The cherub is the bond of the Prime Minds, the order of Pallas, the overseer of contemplative philosophy. First we must emulate him, thirst after him and to the same degree understand him in order that we may be raised …
Hic est nodus primarum mentium, ordo Palladicus philosophiae contemplativae preses

judged.justification: Ties the cherub, the contemplative order and Pallas together, and puts philosophy at the cherubic middle of the ascent.
Grounds the three-stage way of the Oration in Dionysius on the cherubic hosts.

quotes.t: emulating the cherubic life on Earth, curbing the drive of the emotions through moral science, dispersing the darkness of reason through dialectics
Then may we imbue our purified and well-prepared soul with the light of natural philosophy so that afterward we may perfect it with the knowledge of things divine

judged.justification: Maps the Dionysian purgation, illumination and perfection onto moral philosophy, dialectics, natural philosophy and theology.

quotes.t: let us also consult Jacob the patriarch

there is a ladder that stretches from the lowest earth to the highest Heavens and that is marked by a series of many rungs. God is at its height, and the contemplative angels move up and down it in turns
esse scalas ab imo solo ad caeli summa protensas, multorum graduum serie distinctas, fastigio Dominum insidere, contemplatores angelos per eas vicibus alternantes ascendere et descendere
if we are to carry out these things in our efforts to imitate the angelic life, who, I ask, will dare to touch the Ladder of God, either with unclean feet or with unwashed hands
It is unlawful, as the mysteries have it, to touch the clean with the unclean
Once we, inspired by the cherubic spirit, have reached this point through the art of speaking or of reasoning
until at last, resting in the bosom of the Father Who is at the top of the ladder, we shall be made perfect in theological bliss
iam Cherubico spiritu animati, per scalarum idest naturae gradus philosophantes

judged.justification: Makes the ladder of the angels the ladder of the grades of nature, climbed by philosophizing.
States the mediating role of the middle order as a principle and applies it to philosophy between theology and the many.

quotes.t: that peace which God makes in His heavens, which the angels who came down to earth announced to men of good will so that these men would, ascending to heaven, be transformed by it into angels
ut per eam ipsi homines ascendentes in caelum angeli fierent

judged.justification: Names peace, and not only knowledge, as what turns men into angels.
Ties the seraphic state to the frenzy of love and to loss of the self in God.

quotes.t: let us call upon Raphael, the heavenly physician, to set us free with moral philosophy and dialectics, as if with healing drugs
Raphaelem coelestem medicum advocemus, qui nos morali et dialectica uti pharmacis salutaribus liberet

judged.justification: Recasts the three philosophical stages as the offices of three archangels.

quotes.t: Gabriel, the strength of God, will abide in us and, leading us through the marvels of nature and showing us everywhere the merit and the power of God, he will finally deliver us to Michael the high priest, who will …
tandem sacerdoti summo Michaeli nos tradet

judged.justification: Assigns natural philosophy to Gabriel and theology to Michael, completing the archangelic sequence.
Says that angelic forms are the subject matter of the second of the three Kabbalistic disciplines.

quotes.t: of the fall of the demons, of the hierarchy of the angels, of Purgatory, of the punishments in Hell. I saw the same things that we read every day in Paul, Dionysius, Jerome, and Augustine
de casu demonum, de ordinibus angelorum, de purgatoriis, de inferorum paenis eadem legi quae apud Paulum et Dionysium

judged.justification: Claims agreement between the Kabbalistic and the Christian angelology, the ground for reading the two hierarchies together.

bears.note: The note sets Pico's account of man's central place against Ficino's Platonic Theology.

judged.justification: Reads the Oration's opening as a departure from Ficino's static middle position.
Reads the three-rank ladder as the ordering of the three faculties.
Supplies the referent of the clause 'or soon thereafter', which the text leaves unexplained.

bears.note: The editors give Ficino's Theologia Platonica 14.3 as a parallel (cf.).

judged.justification: Isolates the angelic transformation as the one unambiguously positive change in the chameleon passage.

quotes.t: Both Garin and Tognon refer to the Ethiopic Book of Enoch 40.8 (first or second century; see Knibb 1978)
Rather than referring to a single text, Pico more likely elaborates on a complex, and apocryphal, textual tradition. His reference could include the so-called Third Book of Enoch

open.t: Which Enoch text or texts Pico knew is not settled.

quotes.t: The princeps edition has a blank space where the Hebrew word should be. Both Basel editions (1557 and 1572) have Mal'akh ha-Sekinach, Hebrew retroversion of the Latin angelum divinitatis

open.t: What Hebrew word Pico wrote at this point is not fixed by the printed tradition, since the princeps has a blank and the Basel editions supply a back-translation.

rel.basis: supplies a restoration for the blank the printed editions leave

judged.justification: The identification of the name as Metatron rests on a restoration, not on the printed text.

quotes.t: Following Wirszubski (1989, 232), Bausi (Pico 2003, 171–72) restores in his edition the characters found in the earlier version of the Oration (possibly one of two drafts Pico prepared in fall 1486 while in Umbria before moving to Rome) in …

rel.basis: supplies a restoration for the blank the printed editions leave

judged.justification: Makes 'Metatron' a scholarly restoration from a manuscript, so the Enoch-Metatron reading of section 35 depends on the reading of a draft.

quotes.t: A reference to Metatron can be found in Pico's Commento sopra una canzona (written in the same period as the Oration and the Conclusiones, 1486) almost in the exact terms of the Oration, as a synonym of transfiguration

This is what the statement of the Cabalist wise men must mean, when they say that Enoch was transformed into Metatron, angel of divinity, or, in general, that any other man is transformed into an angel

As Scholem writes, “two different traditions have been combined in the figure of Metatron. One relates to the heavenly angel who was created with the creation of the world, or even before, and makes him responsible for performing the most …
A different tradition associates Metatron with Enoch
he who ascended to heaven and was changed from a human being into an angel
It is perhaps not surprising that the identification occupies a prominent place in Pico's Christian Cabala

bears.note: Bausi's reading places Pico with Ficino, Theologia Platonica 17.4, on allegorical transformations.

judged.justification: Shows Pico turning words addressed to fallen angels into an exhortation to ascend to the angelic state.

open.t: What Pico means by the celestial that is to be spurned is not settled.

judged.justification: Turns an exhortation to strive toward the heavens into a call to leave the celestial behind for the otherworldly court.
Locates the first use of 'dignity' in an exhortation to emulate the highest angels.

quotes.t: In accordance with the scheme set out by Pseudo-Dionysius (see §70 of the Oration) and confirmed by St. Thomas (Summa Theologiae 1.108, art. 6) and St. Gregory (In evang. II hom. 34), Pico represents here the three divisions of the …
The fact that Pico specifically calls the cherubim contemplators does not, of course, mean that the seraphim and thrones are not

It has been suggested (Farmer 1998, 346–51) that Pico consciously overlaid the cabalistic sefirot on the celestial hierarchy elucidated by Pseudo-Dionysius. In this arrangement, as it applies here, each of these three types of angels is associated with a specific …

open.t: Whether Pico consciously overlaid the sefirot on the Dionysian ranks is put forward as a suggestion, not established.

judged.justification: If accepted, the three ranks carry Kabbalistic values (love, judgment, intelligence) alongside the Dionysian ones.

quotes.t: This unusual phrase, in which God “broods,” is glossed by Pico himself in Heptaplus 2.2
that is, the closely adhering spiritual Olympus, the seat of the Spirits of the Lord, warmed it with its warmth-giving light
These three classes of angels are known as the “first hierarchy,” as they are closest to God
The “Prime Minds” are the angels; the “Order of Pallas” is a phrase referring to the cherubim, insofar as they preside over the contemplators (Pico 2003, 26–27)

judged.justification: Fixes the Order of Pallas as the cherubim, the contemplative rank.

bears.note: Bausi, as reported, finds Barbaro's language in the Oration's passage on the cherubic life.

quotes.t: Celestial Hierarchy 165b–c, 205c–209d. This Dionysius was, of course, thought to be the homonymous follower of Paul of Acts 17:34
The mystic three-stage path, or triplex via, was often articulated as purgatio-illuminatio-unitio (or perfectio )

borghesi2012:084.hedge_words: Pico may have also been thinking

quotes.t: Interestingly, Pico's depiction of the ... relatively harmonious comings and goings of the angels on the ladder is a rather joyous contradiction of the typical iconography of the ladder to God

judged.justification: Reads the angels' motion on the ladder as harmony against a tradition of struggle.

bears.note: The note gives Ficino's De divino furore as a parallel (cf.) for the ardent seraphim.

quotes.t: On the names of the angels as connected to the doctrine of the sefirot (a connection which might be alluded to through the words “the most hidden mysteries”), see Yates (1979)

judged.justification: Suggests the three archangels' names carry a Kabbalistic sense.

quotes.t: See also §141, “sacerdoti summo Michaeli” in reference to the archangel, whose name in Hebrew translates as “Who is like God?”
Michael with the sefirah Keter (Crown), which he interprets as the symbol of the priesthood

judged.justification: Gives the archangel Michael a place in the sefirotic scheme, beyond the Dionysian one.

quotes.t: See §161 and §§65–66, where “the order of Pallas” is described as that of cherubic contemplation that brings to fruition the link between love (the seraphim) and justice or law (the thrones)

judged.justification: Reads the cherub as joining love and judgment, so Pallas names the mediating rank.

quotes.t: throughout the Oration and Conclusiones, as the personification of Wisdom or Philosophy, Pallas signifies the intellectual nature which leads to wisdom (in Conclusiones 2.5.14 and 2.11.10, the Orphean Pallas is associated with the cabalists' Metatron)

judged.justification: Links the Order of Pallas of section 66 to Metatron, so the cherubic order and the Enoch of section 35 may name one figure.

quotes.t: The three archangels Pico mentions in §135 represent dialectics, natural philosophy, and theology

judged.justification: Dates Pico's turn to the Cabala to the passage on the angelic forms in the earlier redaction.
